newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Postabank sees two capital hikes this year.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Postabank sees two capital hikes this year.

text.p: Postabank, Hungary's second largest commercial bank, plans to increase its capital by about 20 billion forints ($109.9 million) this year in two steps, the bank said on Thursday.
Postabank was hit by a wave of withdrawals of deposits worth some 24 billion forints at the end of February after rumours spread that it could become insolvent.
The bank survived the panic, but the deposit withdrawals cut Postabank's profits and made the need for a capital increase, which the bank began to prepare in November 1996, more pressing.
Postabank Chairman and CEO Gabor Princz told a meeting of the bank's small shareholders that the expansion of Postabank's assets would have made a capital injection necessary anyway.
The bank boosted its balance sheet total by 109.1 billion forints to 378.7 billion in 1996, and the expansion and further development demanded a strengthening of the bank's capital basis, he said.
He added that he expected Hungarian shareholders and certain clients of the bank to raise the 16.45 billion forint registered capital in July.

Negotiations on a second capital increase with potential foreign investors are likely to be completed by the autumn (September-November), he said, adding that the capital hikes would be followed by listing the bank's shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
Both capital increases would be around 10 billion forints, he said.
"We hope that this would elevate the bank to among the most strongly capitalised banks in the country," Princz said.

According to audited figures, the bank posted an after-tax profit of six million forints in 1996, sharply down from some three billion forints published in a preliminary earnings report published before the withdrawals and well below its 1995 pre-tax profit of 2.83 billion forints.
Janos Lakatos, Chairman and General Manager of Postabank's brokerage subsidiary told the shareholders that the fall of the profits was indirectly due to February's withdrawals.

Following the panic, Postabank's auditing company valued the bank's assets more cautiously, and the bank had to place a substantial extra amount in the risk reserves, he said, without disclosing the actual figure.
The government helped Postabank to cover risky assets following the run, by guaranteeing the repayment of 12 billion forints of Postabank's claims.
The National Bank of Hungary eased Postabank's obligations for placing reserves with the central bank so as to help the bank recover from the damages caused by the panic.
Postabank shareholders will hold their annual meeting on Friday. The meeting will elect the members of the supervisory board and the board of directors.
